results.title: Mirae Asset Sekuritas assesses global pressures still weighing on the market
results.body: Mirae Asset Sekuritas says global sentiment continues to weigh on Indonesia’s market, noting that the Jakarta Composite Index (IHSG) fell 1.33% to 6,589 amid a net foreign outflow of Rp748 billion. The pressure was most evident on banking stocks BBCA and BBRI, while foreign investors accumulated commodity‑linked shares such as ANTM, AADI, CUAN and PTBA. The firm cites macro factors including the US 10‑year Treasury yield near 5%, the ECB rate at 2.5%, high oil prices, the rupiah at roughly Rp17,547 per USD and a 10‑year SBN yield of 7.11% as limiting the transmission of global yields to the domestic market. Despite these headwinds, consumer confidence rose to 118.5 in August and Mirae Asset recommends a selective portfolio focused on strong fundamentals and solid cash flow.

results.title: PT Pembangunan Perumahan Tbk signs Master Restructuring Agreement to restructure Rp18.2 trillion debt with four state-owned banks
results.body: PT Pembangunan Perumahan Tbk signed a Master Restructuring Agreement on 10 September 2026 to restructure its Rp18.2 trillion debt with four state‑owned banks. The debt is divided into three tranches: Tranche A of about Rp13.33 trillion at 3.5% per year (1% cash quarterly and 2.5% deferred to 2041) to be repaid over 15 years via a balloon payment; Tranche B of about Rp4.05 trillion at 1% per year with a five‑year bullet payment funded by divestment proceeds; and Tranche C covering accrued interest from the standstill period, repaid in interest‑free installments over 18 months. The participating lenders are PT Bank Mandiri Tbk (acting as Facility Agent), PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk, PT Bank Negara Indonesia Tbk and PT Bank Syariah Indonesia Tbk. Certain working‑capital facilities tied to project owners are excluded from the restructuring and will be serviced independently of project cash flows.

results.title: PTPP Restructures Rp18.2 Trillion Debt, Detailing Payment Schemes
results.body: PT PP (Persero) Tbk (PTPP) has restructured Rp18.2 trillion of debt into three tranches: Tranche A (Rp13.33 trillion) with a 15‑year balloon payment and 3.5% interest, Tranche B (Rp4.05 trillion) with a five‑year bullet payment and 1% interest, and Tranche C covering interest or profit‑share accrued since the stand‑still, paid over 18 months. The restructuring, governed by a Master Restructuring Agreement signed on 10 September 2026 with PT Bank Mandiri (Persero) Tbk, PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia (Persero) Tbk, PT Bank Negara Indonesia (Persero) Tbk, and PT Bank Syariah Indonesia (Persero) Tbk, will take effect after a shareholders’ meeting. PTPP aims to transform its business and finances to sustain operations, improve performance, and repay creditors. The agreement also excludes certain working‑capital facilities, which remain independent of project cash flows.

results.title: PT PP Tbk signs Rp18.2 trillion debt restructuring agreement with four state‑owned banks
results.body: PT PP Tbk entered into a Master Restructuring Agreement on 10 September 2026 to restructure Rp18.2 trillion of debt with four state‑owned banks. The agreement, in which PT Bank Mandiri Tbk acts as the facility agent and PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk, PT Bank Negara Indonesia Tbk and PT Bank Syariah Indonesia Tbk serve as lenders, splits the debt into Tranche A of about Rp13.33 trillion at 3.5% annual interest (1% cash quarterly, 2.5% deferred to 2041), Tranche B of about Rp4.05 trillion at 1% annual interest with bullet repayment over five years, and Tranche C covering interest accrued from the stand‑still period with interest‑free repayments over 18 months. Repayment of Tranche A will be made over 15 years with a balloon payment, while Tranche B’s repayment is sourced from divestments, and Tranche C’s installments are independent of project cash flows. The restructuring becomes effective after the shareholders’ meeting and fulfillment of the conditions set out in the MRA, and is intended to support PT PP’s business and financial transformation and ensure its ability to service all creditors.

results.title: Indonesian government allocates Rp11 trillion to Bank Rakyat Indonesia and Bank Syariah Indonesia for a program giving citizens Rp50,000 opening balances
results.body: The Indonesian government announced a program to open bank accounts for up to 200 million citizens with an initial Rp50,000 balance, funded by an Rp11 trillion allocation from the state budget (APBN). The accounts will be provided through the two state‑owned banks, Bank Rakyat Indonesia and Bank Syariah Indonesia. Implementation will be coordinated with Bank Indonesia, the Financial Services Authority and the civil registration agency to enable automatic account creation, and the funding may be drawn from the 2026 or 2027 APBN. The rollout will be phased, and the initial balance will be withdrawable by account holders.

results.title: BSI Ready to Provide Bank Accounts for All Indonesian Citizens as Directed by President Prabowo
results.body: PT Bank Syariah Indonesia Tbk (BSI) has announced it is prepared to open bank accounts for all Indonesian citizens in line with President Prabowo Subianto’s directive, partnering with Bank Rakyat Indonesia to roll out the program. BSI, a national Islamic bank, reported a net profit of Rp4.16 trillion in the first half of 2026, up 11% year‑over‑year, and third‑party funds of Rp393 trillion, up 22%. The bank’s customer base reached 24.3 million as of June 2026, following a 9.84‑million increase since its 2021 merger. The government will fund each new account with Rp50,000, with no fees, and the accounts will also serve as a channel for social assistance disbursements.

results.title: IHSG falls 0.58% in first session as foreign investors net sell Rp577 billion, led by PT Bank Central Asia Tbk and PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk
results.body: The Jakarta Composite Index (IHSG) declined 0.58% to 6,647.50 in the first trading session on Wednesday (9/9), with total transaction value reaching Rp8.32 trillion. Foreign investors recorded a net sell of Rp577.21 billion, dominated by bank stocks with the largest market capitalization. PT Bank Central Asia Tbk posted the largest net foreign sell of Rp419.03 billion, followed by PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk at Rp62.73 billion. Most sectoral indices weakened, with healthcare down 1.45% and technology down 1%, while transportation gained 2.15%. Regional Asian markets were mixed, with South Korea's KOSPI rising 1.01% and India's NIFTY falling 0.52%.

results.title: Summary of stock recommendations for 8 September 2026 from seven Indonesian securities firms.
results.body: The article summarizes stock recommendations issued by seven Indonesian securities firms for Tuesday, 8 September 2026, following a 0.25% decline in the IHSG to 6,619 on Monday. The index fell amid weakness in financial, raw material, and technology sectors, which dropped 0.75%, 0.71%, and 0.61% respectively, with trading volume of 37.05 billion shares worth Rp13.73 trillion. The brokers recommended a total of 24 stocks: IMPC, TINS, KOTA from BRI Danareksa Sekuritas; SSIA, ADRO, BBRI, ERAA, COCO, COIN from BNI Sekuritas; HMSP, MDIA from Phillip Sekuritas; HRUM, INKP, MDKA, TPIA from MNC Sekuritas; HMSP, INDF, BTPS, TAPG, CMRY, BUMI from CGS International Sekuritas; INDF, INKP, AKRA, BFIN, MNCN from Phintraco Sekuritas; and ADRO, DEWA, INKP from Mirae Asset Sekuritas. Several stocks, including HMSP, INKP, ADRO, and INDF, were recommended by multiple firms.

results.title: IHSG forecast to reach 6,700 amid Anak Krakatau eruption concerns, with BBCA, BBRI, BMRI under pressure and BRI Danareksa Sekuritas recommending IMPC, TINS, KOTA, UDNG.
results.body: The article forecasts that Indonesia's composite index (IHSG) could climb to the 6,600‑6,700 range, with a key resistance at 6,700, despite the ongoing Anak Krakatau eruption. On Monday the index slipped 0.25% to 6,619.67, staying above the 20‑day moving average and with a positive MACD, while foreign‑exchange reserves rose to US$146.5 billion supporting domestic sentiment. Technical pressure is coming from BBCA, BBRI and BMRI, whereas BRI Danareksa Sekuritas recommends swing‑trade positions in IMPC and TINS, a day‑trade in KOTA, and a sell stance on UDNG. The market’s near‑term direction may be swayed by the U.S. CPI release on 11 September, projected at 3.4% headline and 2.4% core inflation, which could affect risk appetite and the index’s trajectory.

results.title: IHSG Projected to Remain Limited on Tuesday (Sept 8), Sentiment Overview
results.body: The Jakarta Composite Index (IHSG) is projected to trade within a limited range on Tuesday (Sept 8) after closing at 6,619.67, down 16.80 points (0.25%) on Monday, with analysts noting pressure from big‑cap financial stocks BBCA, BBRI and BMRI while health and energy sectors provide support and technical levels suggest support near 6,603‑6,600 and resistance near 6,632‑6,700. Analysts from MNC Sekuritas and BRI Danareksa Sekuritas set target prices for HRUM (Rp 985‑1,015), INKP (Rp 9,250‑9,500), MDKA (Rp 2,980‑3,020) and recommend buying IMPC (Rp 1,605‑1,730), TINS (Rp 4,610‑4,830) and KOTA (Rp 224‑236) as the market watches upcoming NFP, China trade‑balance and US CPI releases and Indonesia’s foreign‑exchange reserves at US$146.5 billion.

results.title: Foreign investors show early signs of tactical re-entry into Indonesian equities, with analysts highlighting big banks and select sectors.
results.body: Foreign investors are showing early signs of tactical re-entry into Indonesian stocks, with net buying concentrated in large-cap banks during the week of August 31 to September 4, 2026. In that period, foreign net purchases reached Rp1.85–2.3 trillion, led by PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk, PT Bank Central Asia Tbk, PT Bank Mandiri Tbk, and PT Bank Negara Indonesia Tbk, which together recorded over Rp3.19 trillion of net foreign buying in the regular market. LQ45 outflows have declined sharply from over Rp15 trillion in June to under Rp2 trillion in August, and the number of LQ45 stocks with outflows fell to 27 from 36 in June. Analysts caution this is not yet a structural trend reversal, as year-to-date foreign outflows remain around US$3.94 billion, and sustainability depends on Federal Reserve policy, rupiah stability, and earnings growth. Potential rotation targets include commodity stocks ANTM, AMMN, and INCO, as well as consumer and industrial names TLKM, ASII, INDF, and UNTR, with advisors recommending accumulation on weakness.

results.title: PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk announces dividend payout ratio to fall to about 70% for FY 2026, reaffirming commitment to shareholder returns
results.body: PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk said its dividend payout ratio will be reduced to roughly 70% for the 2026 fiscal year while reaffirming its commitment to delivering optimal shareholder returns. The announcement was made by Finance & Strategy Director Achmad Royadi, who noted that the payout policy will balance fundamentals, capital needs and long‑term growth, with a long‑term target range of 50‑60%. The bank reported consolidated net profit of Rp 31.2 trillion for the first half of 2026, up 17.5% YoY, alongside credit growth of 16.2% YoY, an NPL ratio improving to 2.9% and a capital adequacy ratio of 21.5%, above its 20% target. The lower payout follows a 92% ratio in 2025 and reflects PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk’s strong fundamentals that allow it to balance shareholder returns with capital reinforcement for future expansion.

results.title: Foreign Capital Flow to IHSG Intensifies, Up 8 Times Last Week
results.body: Foreign investors’ net buying in the Indonesian stock market surged eightfold last week, with the benchmark index rising 1.82% to 6,636. The bulk of the inflow targeted the country’s largest banks—BBRI, BMRI, BBCA and BBNI—where net purchases reached about Rp1.6 trillion in the regular market during the week of August 24‑28. Over the past month, foreign investors accumulated net purchases of Rp4.64 trillion across all markets, while the banks posted strong first‑semester earnings of Rp31.2 trillion, Rp30.4 trillion, Rp29.5 trillion and Rp10.8 trillion respectively. Credit growth outpaced deposit growth, tightening liquidity and underscoring the importance of monitoring NIM and bank liquidity amid continued foreign inflows.

results.title: Foreign investors heavily bought BBRI shares and sold CPIN and BRMS in the week of August 31–September 4, 2026.
results.body: Foreign investor trading activity in Indonesian stocks for the week of August 31–September 4, 2026 showed net buying overall, with the IHSG rising 1.82% to 6,636.47. Foreign investors recorded a net buy of Rp2.3 trillion across the market, reducing the year-to-date net sell in the regular market to Rp96.11 trillion. The largest net buy was in PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk at Rp1.43 trillion, driving its share price up 6.27% to Rp3,390. The largest net sell was in PT Charoen Pokphand Indonesia Tbk at Rp516.62 billion, though its share price still rose 4.91% to Rp3,210. BRMS also saw significant foreign selling, according to the report.

results.title: Foreign investors heavily buy big bank stocks PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk, PT Bank Central Asia Tbk and PT Bank Mandiri Tbk in the past week.
results.body: The article reports that foreign investors returned to Indonesia’s banking sector last week, posting the largest net purchases in the market for the three big banks. PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk recorded a net buy of Rp 1.41 trillion, PT Bank Central Asia Tbk Rp 1.20 trillion and PT Bank Mandiri Tbk Rp 1.01 trillion, together accounting for about Rp 3.62 trillion of foreign inflows, while PT Bank Negara Indonesia Tbk added Rp 261.39 billion. Other heavily bought stocks included PT Chandra Asri Pacific Tbk (Rp 238.84 billion), PT Dian Swastatika Sentosa Tbk (Rp 168.05 billion), PT Triputra Agro Persada Tbk (Rp 147.58 billion), PT Erajaya Swasembada Tbk (Rp 126.94 billion), PT Adaro Andalan Indonesia Tbk (Rp 93.49 billion) and PT Alamtri Resources Indonesia Tbk (Rp 84.23 billion). Foreign investors sold PT Charoen Pokphand Indonesia Tbk (Rp 485.66 billion), PT Merdeka Gold Resources Tbk (Rp 337.42 billion), PT Indosat Tbk (Rp 225.62 billion), PT Amman Mineral Internasional Tbk (Rp 173 billion), PT Petrosea Tbk (Rp 162.7 billion), PT Astra International Tbk (Rp 150.28 billion), PT Bukalapak.com Tbk (Rp 129.03 billion), PT Bumi Resources Minerals Tbk (Rp 126.97 billion), PT Indo Tambangraya Megah Tbk (Rp 121.57 billion) and PT Unilever Indonesia Tbk (Rp 109.91 billion), contributing to a total foreign net buy of Rp 1.85 trillion and supporting a 1.82 % weekly rise in the IHSG index, which closed at 6,636.47, down 31.4 points (0.47 %) on Friday.

results.title: Popular News Roundup: CPIN Earnings Surge, Strong Foreign Buying in BBCA, BBRI and BUMI, and Steady Gold Jewelry Prices
results.body: The roundup highlights PT Charoen Pokphand Indonesia Tbk’s Q2 2026 net profit soaring 211% YoY to IDR 1.13 trillion while trading at a PER of 7.18×, and strong foreign inflows into PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (IDR 820.2 bn net buy), PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk (IDR 1.4 trn net buy) and PT Bumi Resources Tbk (IDR 83.2 bn net buy) with target price upside of 41.5% for BBCA and a PBV of 1.9× for BBRI. Gold jewelry prices across various karats remained steady, as reported by Raja Emas Indonesia, Hartadinata Abadi and Laku Emas.

results.title: PT Bank Central Asia Tbk, PT Bank Mandiri Tbk, PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk, and PT Bank Negara Indonesia Tbk Report Combined Rp 111.67 Trillion Profit
results.body: PT Bank Central Asia Tbk, PT Bank Mandiri Tbk, PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk, and PT Bank Negara Indonesia Tbk, the four largest banks in Indonesia and members of the KBMI 4 group, posted a combined net profit of Rp 111.67 trillion for January–July 2026, an 8.73% year‑on‑year increase. In the same period they expanded credit to Rp 5,017.30 trillion (up 16.95% yoy, representing 55.93% of national credit) and total deposits to Rp 5,693.98 trillion (up 15.71% yoy, accounting for 58.90% of total deposits), outpacing industry averages of 13.0% and 7.7% respectively.

results.title: BRI Shares Flooded with Funds, Entering a New Phase
results.body: Foreign investors net bought Rp 1.4 trillion of PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk shares in the week of 31 August–4 September 2026, making BRI the most purchased stock on the Indonesia Stock Exchange. The buying occurred in the regular market, and BRI’s share price closed at Rp 3,390, down 0.59% on Friday, while the stock rose 6.2% over the week and 12.2% over the month. MNC Sekuritas and Pluang Maju Sekuritas each reaffirmed a buy rating on BRI with a target price of Rp 4,050, reflecting a price‑to‑book value of 1.9× for 2026 and 1.8× for 2027 and citing strong pre‑provision operating profit growth, cost‑efficiency, and a planned reduction in payout ratio. Risks noted include slower credit growth, weaker macro conditions, and heightened competition in the wholesale segment.

results.title: PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk reports Q2 2026 net profit of Rp31.2 trillion amid healthy expansion
results.body: PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk reported a consolidated net profit of Rp31.2 trillion for the second quarter of 2026, up 17.5% year‑on‑year, with total assets reaching Rp2,352 trillion, a rise of 11.7% YoY. Credit disbursement grew 16.2% YoY to Rp1,646 trillion while key asset‑quality ratios improved, with the non‑performing loan ratio falling to 2.9% from 3.0%, the loan‑at‑risk ratio improving to 9.1% from 9.6%, and the cost of credit decreasing to 3.1% from 3.4%. The bank attributes the results to its selective growth strategy, disciplined risk management and a diversified UMKM‑focused portfolio that keeps expansion within its risk appetite.

results.title: Foreign investors' top ten net‑buy stocks on 4 Sep 2026 amid a 0.47% IHSG correction
results.body: The article reports that foreign investors net bought ten Indonesian stocks on Friday 4 Sep 2026 while the Jakarta Composite Index (IHSG) corrected 0.47% to 6,636.47. The market closed within a range of 6,633–6,704, with total share volume of 35.8 billion and transaction value of Rp 15.04 trillion, and foreign investors recorded a net sell of Rp 29.80 billion that day. Over the week, foreign investors accumulated a net buy of Rp 1.85 trillion, and the ten most purchased stocks were PT Dian Swastatika Sentosa Tbk (Rp 196.83 billion), PT Timah Tbk (Rp 158.76 billion), PT Adaro Andalan Indonesia Tbk (Rp 46.47 billion), PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk (Rp 33.6 billion), PT Chandra Daya Investasi Tbk (Rp 25.27 billion), PT Bank Negara Indonesia Tbk (Rp 24.54 billion), PT Merdeka Gold Resources Tbk (Rp 24.45 billion), PT Bukit Asam Tbk (Rp 19.11 billion), PT Sumber Global Energy Tbk (Rp 13.25 billion) and PT United Tractors Tbk (Rp 10.43 billion). These companies were directly impacted by the foreign investors' net purchases, while the IHSG still posted a weekly gain of 1.82% despite the weekend correction.
